proposals.before: Lang said, "To abandon my uncle's heir thus and die together leaves no regret."
proposals.after: Lang said, "How could I bear to leave my uncle like this? Dying together leaves no regret."
proposals.reason: Chinese 忍季父如此 means bearing to leave the uncle (季父) in such a state, not "uncle's heir".

proposals.before: Lang said, "To bear my uncle's heir thus and die together leaves no regret."
proposals.after: Lang said, "How could I bear my uncle like this? Dying together leaves no regret."
proposals.reason: Chinese 忍季父如此 refers to the uncle (季父), not an heir.

proposals.before: Though I lack talent, I am scarcely inferior to those who advanced Jiu Jiu or welcomed Shu Diao and Yiya to court.
proposals.after: Though I lack talent, I am scarcely inferior to those who advanced Jiu Jiu or welcomed Shu Diao and Tou Xu to court.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 頭須 (Tou Xu), not 易牙 (Yiya); literal English already has Tou Xu.

decisions.reason: 朗曰「忍季父如此，俱死無恨」: 季父 is the uncle (Xian), not an "uncle's heir"; rhetorical 忍…如此 rejects abandoning him in that plight. The replacement restores that sense and fits the preceding 吾兒去矣.
Same Chinese 忍季父如此: 季父 means uncle, not heir. The proposed literal correctly drops "uncle's heir" and keeps the rhetorical bearing of 忍.
納豎刁、頭須 names Tou Xu (頭須), not Yiya (易牙). Replacing Yiya with Tou Xu matches the Chinese and the already-correct literal.
